item.title: Second passing point?, 24th November
item.description:
It was recently reported that a much needed second passing point had been established on school road What has in fact been done is double yellow lines places opposite the existing single yellows With so many schools close by this road gets very busy and you can only one vehicle down or up at a time If cars have already passed the point at the bottom of the road nearest the high street then there is nowhere else to pull in to let someone pass Meaning cars are having to reverse a large distance in order to let someone through Surely a second point maybe located here by the bin would ease this? With so many young children walking down this road on a daily basis surely their safety needs to be thought about and cars reversing does not help this

item.title: COMPLAINT – Serious Ongoing Problems in Our Building.Woodsford Portland Street London., 23rd November
item.description:
URGENT FORMAL COMPLAINT – Serious Ongoing Problems in Our Building.Woodsford Portland Street London. Dear Management Team, I am writing to make a formal complaint about the ongoing and increasingly unacceptable problems in our building. Residents have been reporting these issues almost every day, but unfortunately, nothing seems to be improving. We are extremely frustrated and disappointed with the current management and the lack of action from the officer responsible for looking after our building. The problems include: Lifts constantly breaking down: The lifts are repeatedly out of service. They are repaired one day, only to break down again the following day. This has been happening for years, and residents cannot continue living with this situation. Dog urine throughout the building: Some dog owners are allowing their dogs to urinate inside the lifts. Unfortunately, this behaviour has now spread to the staircases, corridors and other communal areas. There is a terrible smell, and the building is becoming increasingly unhygienic and unpleasant for everyone. Lack of CCTV: We desperately need CCTV cameras installed in communal areas to help identify those responsible for damaging and misusing shared spaces and to discourage this behaviour. We urgently request the following action: A new building management officer who is willing to take responsibility and deal with residents' concerns. A proper investigation into why the lifts keep breaking down, followed by a permanent solution rather than temporary repairs. CCTV installation in appropriate communal areas. Regular cleaning and proper monitoring of the building. Action against residents who allow their dogs to urinate in communal areas. A meeting with residents and the management team to discuss these serious concerns. We have reached a point where sending letters and making daily complaints is simply not enough. We need people who are prepared to take responsib
